title: Henry Allen's funeral band, Didn't He Ramble and Kelly's tone
summary: Playing funerals for Henry Allen across the river; Kelly's big tone on the street and softer for dances.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. I played with a guy across the river and he had a funeral you'd better know how to read when you go there. That was old man Henry Allen. Oh, yes. You played Henry Allen's band then, too. You heard him, man. Yeah, he had nothing but real funeral march. Yeah. That Flea's a Bird. I done played at him many times. Oh, then. Didn't he ramble? That was Chris' place when he turned you loose when he's coming back. That was his piece. Didn't he ramble? Ramble come to put his cutting down.
Well, did he... I guess he wouldn't use his boots on a parade.
Oh, not for no parade, no. Uh-uh. Need all the air you could get in there for a parade.
Now, was he in a pretty big tone loud or was he soft on the... on the brakes?
No, he was a kind of stout player, a connet player. Pretty big tone. Yeah. Yeah. It was kind of stout.
But he, uh, I suppose for dances he'd come down soft sometimes?
Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. You had to come down. I didn't like that kind of... blowing your head off all the way through. Coming with some kind of harmony. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Get on low.
